sections.overview: The Terek sandpiper is a migratory shorebird that breeds in Eurasia and winters farther south.
sections.identification: Its long, slightly upturned bill and short orange-yellow legs are distinctive.
sections.habitat: Outside the breeding season it uses coastal mudflats, estuaries, beaches and mangroves.
sections.diet: It pecks or probes in wet mud for insects, small molluscs and crustaceans.
sections.behavior: It migrates over long distances and may gather at high-tide roosts with other waders.
sections.reproduction: It nests in a shallow ground scrape in northern forest valleys or tundra; breeding occurs in spring and early summer.
sections.ecology: The Singapore account records it as a passage migrant and winter visitor.
sections.conservation: The 2016 IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern; loss and change of wetlands are noted pressures.
